In scientific literature, such a problem has been addressed both with statistical models and neural networks (NN) to perform sensor prediction, while keeping the user in full control of the robot's motion. hidden_assumptions: Object identity is independent of the robot hand or end-effector. | The sensor stream is a sufficient statistic for object identity regardless of action. | Multi-modal fusion improves identity without modeling which modality is action-gated.
variables_treated_as_fixed: end-effector morphology; probing action family; available contact observables; deployment embodiment/domain
failure_modes_ignored: same object labels collapse or split when the gripper changes; visually identical objects differ only through contact; unmodeled probing choices hide discriminative variables; success/failure semantics differ across suction, pinch, and enveloping grasps
what_it_makes_less_novel: Contributes background pressure but does not directly close gripper-dependent identity.
what_it_leaves_open: formal equivalence classes induced by gripper-action observation channels; morphology-indexed object identity rather than embodiment-invariant labels

title: Bayesian and Neural Inference on LSTM-Based Object Recognition From Tactile and Kinesthetic Information
problem_claimed: Use contact/touch signals to recognize, localize, or manipulate objects when vision is incomplete.
hidden_assumptions: Tactile readings are sensor features rather than gripper-object relational events. | Object mass, friction, compliance, and geometry are separable from the grasp family. | Contact observables reveal intrinsic object state rather than a quotient of state by probe. | A category label is stable across changes in contact geometry. | Benchmark labels correspond to the distinctions a deployed gripper can observe.
variables_treated_as_fixed: end-effector morphology; probing action family; contact sensor layout/calibration; label ontology; deployment embodiment/domain
failure_modes_ignored: same object labels collapse or split when the gripper changes; unmodeled probing choices hide discriminative variables; success/failure semantics differ across suction, pinch, and enveloping grasps; non-identifiability is mistaken for estimator uncertainty
what_it_makes_less_novel: Makes tactile object recognition less novel; leaves morphology-conditioned identity partitions mostly open.
what_it_leaves_open: formal equivalence classes induced by gripper-action observation channels; morphology-indexed object identity rather than embodiment-invariant labels; when tactile signatures are gripper-specific rather than object-intrinsic
